summary: The test-only candidate fully implements the original issue's bounded isolated-process, fresh-cache, process-group kill, and one-retry mitigation. Request changes only because the PR body omits the required current mirror issue URL https://github.com/amdpilot-org/sglang/issues/1008.

tests.what_was_measured: Actual registered cold-cache JIT path on the recorded base; hipcc targeted gfx950 but the NVIDIA-only source failed to find cuda_bf16.h, so no kernel executed.
Exact candidate regressions; 3 passed, including invocation of the registered MXFP4 file with a stalled first attempt and successful retry.
Independent terminal-boundary case: both attempts used distinct fresh caches, timed out, and had their process groups killed before bounded exit 124.
A live production build-lock holder still blocks a waiter indefinitely; the candidate contains this at the registered-test supervisor boundary.
Environment limitation: the mandated prepared interpreter does not contain the ruff module.

gpu_execution.evidence: AMD Instinct MI350X gfx950 was visible and the real JIT invoked hipcc with --offload-arch=gfx950:sramecc+:xnack-, but compilation stopped at missing NVIDIA cuda_bf16.h before any MXFP4 kernel execution.

remaining_counterexamples: The exact intermittent H200 stall was not statistically reproduced because the assigned device is AMD gfx950, not NVIDIA H200.
The production _build_lock intentionally remains unbounded while its owner is alive; only this registered test is bounded by the new supervisor.
The candidate regression validates supervisor mechanics but its self-test worker exits before executing the MXFP4 JIT or GPU kernel path.
The candidate PR body omits the required current mirror issue URL https://github.com/amdpilot-org/sglang/issues/1008.
remaining_limitations: The NVIDIA-specific MXFP4 source cannot compile on the assigned AMD gfx950 host because cuda_bf16.h is unavailable.
No MXFP4 GPU numerical output was produced.
Ruff is absent from the mandated prepared Python environment.
